0.0.n: A borrowed English word used as a noun.

0.1.n: Marks lunch as the topic of the sentence.

0.2.n: The ending め softens 軽い, suggesting a somewhat smaller amount.

0.3.n: Makes 軽め describe how the speaker eats.

0.4.n: The て-form of 食べる links eating with taking a break.

0.6.n: Emphasizes taking a sufficient, restful break rather than a token pause.

0.7.n: Pairs with 取る to describe taking time to rest.

0.8.n: Marks 休憩 as what the speaker takes.

0.9.n: The plain form modifies こと as part of the action the speaker keeps in mind.

0.10.n: Turns the preceding actions into a noun phrase that can be marked with を.

0.11.n: Marks the whole action phrase ending in こと as what the speaker consciously focuses on.

0.12.n: 意識する plus ています politely expresses an ongoing conscious effort.

1.0.n: 中 attaches to リモートワーク to indicate time spent doing that activity.

1.1.n: Marks remote-working time as when the following situation applies.

1.2.n: Highlights remote-working time as the topic, potentially contrasting it with other times.

1.3.n: With する, this noun describes doing household tasks.

1.4.n: Marks 家事 as the activity being done.

1.5.n: The plain form comes before と to introduce a condition.

1.6.n: Links doing chores to the predictable result of getting tired.

1.7.n: Describes the degree of tiredness as substantial.

1.8.n: The plain form describes a recurring result here, not a single past event.

1.9.n: Gives the reason for the decision stated in the next line.

2.0.n: 中 attaches to 勤務 to indicate being on duty.

2.1.n: Sets working hours as the topic and scope of the rule.

2.2.n: Refers to household tasks the speaker avoids while on duty.

2.3.n: Marks 家事 as what the speaker chooses not to do.

2.4.n: The plain negative form of する states the action being ruled out.

2.5.n: Marks しない as the content of the decision, rather than introducing a condition.

2.6.n: 決める plus ています politely presents a decision that remains in effect.

0.lit: As for lunch, eating lightly and taking a proper break are things I consciously keep in mind.
0.tip: ことを意識しています expresses making a conscious effort to do the actions before こと.

1.lit: During remote work, when I do housework, I get quite tired, so…
1.tip: Verb plus と presents a predictable result: doing chores leads to tiredness.

2.lit: During work hours, I have decided that I will not do housework.
2.tip: Here と marks what was decided; unlike the previous line’s と, it does not mean when.
